A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ViewMask-1-to-3 with the same authors and core framework. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B, including relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original multiview generation and reconstruction experiments on GSO and 3D-FUTURE, mask-schedule ablations, and qualitative task demonstrations, including appendix comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original multiview experiments and ablations and additionally reports its own GenEval results in Table 4 and expanded qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The MAGVIT-v2 tokenization, unified view sequences, three training stages, random masking, cross-entropy objective, and confidence-based predict–remask inference remain unchanged. The revised training corpus and removed turn-style implementation description do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v2 adds GenEval evaluation of compositional text-to-image generation, covering object counts, colors, positions, and attribute binding beyond v1's qualitative T2I examples. Section 3.3 also changes the reported pretraining corpus from ImageNet plus LLaVA CC3M data to ImageNet-based pairs alone. The multiview training sources and GSO/3D-FUTURE coverage remain.

E2.justification: New Table 4 introduces 15 text-to-image comparators, including MMaDA, Show-o, SANA-1.5, and DALL-E 3. Figure 5 adds SPAD to the MV-Adapter/TRELLIS T2MV comparison previously shown in v1's appendix. Comparator membership within Tables 1 and 2 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The new GenEval experiment introduces category-specific and overall compositional-generation scores. Existing multiview rendering, reconstruction metrics, training settings, and 20-step sampling are retained. The hardware and optimization paragraph moves to Appendix A.2 without a setting change; the newly stated pretraining count is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds reconstructed-mesh insets and highlights geometric failures, supplementing image comparisons with qualitative inspection of reconstructed geometry. The linear, quadratic, and cosine masking analysis in Section 4.3, Figure 6, and Table 3 is unchanged. Existing furniture examples are redistributed across the main text and appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experiments. The additional GenEval scores retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds GenEval results, including ViewMask's overall 0.72 versus MMaDA's 0.63 and SANA-1.5's 0.72. Table 1 replaces all six ViewMask image-quality scores: for example, GSO PSNR changes from 20.6112 to 20.3868 and average rank from 1.3 to 1.7. The revised pretraining description prevents treating these as controlled same-setting performance changes. Tables 2 and 3 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The tokenization and embedding definitions, masking formulation, sequence templates, and cross-entropy equation retain the same mathematics. Neither version supplies additional theorems, proofs, or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The core claims about discrete multiview generation and architectural simplicity remain. The abstract and contribution list newly assert a 10.6% IoU advantage on 3D-FUTURE, extending the earlier emphasis on average image-quality rankings. The introduction also moderates the contribution framing toward a systematic exploration.

C2.justification: v2 removes the TRELLIS platform-removal explanation and the appendix's projection-based interpretation of MV-Adapter's qualitative shortcomings. Specific limitations concerning elevation and few viewpoints become general future-work statements about viewpoint diversity. GenEval results receive a new interpretation supporting unified-generation potential. The background-removal caveat remains in Appendix A.3.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 1.2 million pretraining image-caption pairs. It removes v1 Appendix B.3's two-pass turn-style procedure, including object-view generation, background reconstruction, and output fusion. Hardware, batch size, learning rate, optimization, and sampling details are retained after relocation to Appendix A.2.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially reframes the relationship to continuous and 3D methods around exploring a complementary discrete paradigm. Section 2.1 expands discussion of existing joint-view generation, adding One-2-3-45 and MV-AR. GenEval comparisons broaden positioning against generation-only and unified models, while several earlier references, including LLaVA and Dream 7B, are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the introduction are rewritten, with further revisions to related work, task-extension discussion, and the conclusion. Experimental settings move into the appendix, and appendix subsections are reorganized. This constitutes substantial narrative editing despite the stable method exposition.

P2.justification: v2 revises Figure 1, reorganizes furniture comparisons with new mesh insets, and moves the expanded T2MV comparison into Figure 5. It removes the projection diagram and Table 1's Control column, adds GenEval Table 4, and changes the appendix to a single-column layout.

improvement.justification: GenEval results, the SPAD comparison, and mesh visualizations strengthen empirical support. However, v2 removes turn-style reproduction instructions and specific qualifications, while its new 10.6% IoU claim lacks an identified comparator; unchanged Table 2 reports 0.5315 versus the strongest listed baseline's 0.5271. These gains in evidence and losses in transparency leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
